clue.text: Fletcher or Arkwright heard song of Venice

indicators.note: heard tells us the phrase is spoken, and its sound gives the spelling we enter

parts.note: both were parts played by comedian Ronnie Barker, so either is a Barker role

explanation.surface: Someone named Fletcher or Arkwright seems to have been overheard singing a Venetian tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Fletcher was Ronnie Barker's prisoner in the sitcom Porridge and Arkwright his shopkeeper in Open All Hours, both British TV comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarolle is the traditional song of the Venetian gondoliers, so it is a song of Venice.

clue.text: Hope perhaps to secure money, lot of money

indicators.note: to secure means the first piece holds the second fast inside it

parts.note: Bob Hope, the comedian, is an example of a Bob

explanation.surface: Hope as a strategy for getting cash, yielding a great deal of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, costing a bomb means costing a fortune, so the word is slang for a huge sum.

clue.text: Music style Cambridge college served up in fashion

indicators.note: in places the turned college inside the word for fashion

parts.note: a rage is a craze or fashion

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A Cambridge college dining hall is serving up something that is in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge is not the English one here: it is Cambridge, Massachusetts, home of MIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is a syncopated piano style popular around 1900, a genre of music.

clue.text: Decrepit canon stumbling like Frank Spencer

indicators.note: stumbling suggests something tottering out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An aged clergyman tottering about, compared to a famously clumsy sitcom character.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank Spencer is the bumbling hero of the British sitcom Some Mothers Do 'Ave 'Em, forever causing mishaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Spencer is the classic example of someone always having mishaps, a perpetually clumsy person.

clue.text: Decree to remove current munitions

indicators.note: to remove means the second piece is taken out of the first

parts.note: an ordinance is a decree or authoritative order
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An order issued to withdraw the existing stock of weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is military supplies, especially artillery and ammunition, so munitions collectively.

clue.text: Destructive creature mostly in place

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: the locust swarms and devastates crops

explanation.surface: A destructive pest has mostly settled in one spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Locus is Latin for a place or position, used in English for a site or location.

clue.text: Vulcanian site or, alternately, Neptunian

indicators.note: alternately means every other letter is taken, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: A geology debate: is a rock formation volcanic or water-laid, Vulcanian versus Neptunian theory?
explanation.walkthrough: Neptunism and Vulcanism (Plutonism) were rival eighteenth-century theories of rock formation, which gives the surface its sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulcan was the Roman god of fire, and this Sicilian volcano is a fitting home for him, a place of volcanic action.

clue.text: Beat fellow touching

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat or thrash them
a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: Someone thrashing a man is a moving thing to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a tangent line just touches a curve, and the word as adjective means touching.

clue.text: Cat has deep lumps on tip of nose

parts.note: the deep is the abyss, the depths of the sea
inia is the plural of inion, the bony bump at the back of the skull

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cat with deep bumps on the end of its nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The Abyssinian is a short-haired breed of domestic feline from Ethiopia.

clue.text: Computer checking soldier's spelling

indicators.note: checking here means holding back or stopping, so the computer encloses the soldier

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A computer running a spell-check on a soldier's writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelling here means casting spells, sorcery, not orthography.

clue.text: Decline in sporting behaviour around the present era

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: decency is fair, sporting behaviour
AD, Anno Domini, labels the present era of dates

explanation.surface: A lament that fair play has declined in modern times.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadency is moral or cultural decay, a decline from former standards.

clue.text: Rum's ingredient in drunken marauder's rage

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters reel about and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Rum is blamed for fuelling a drunken pirate's fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is distilled from sugar-cane products, and Demerara, from Guyana, is a cane sugar linked with it.

clue.text: Marine nudism rampant when it's hot lately

indicators.note: rampant suggests running wild, so the letters are let loose and rearranged

parts.note: the words as printed are one S short of the thirteen letters needed; the corrected online clue read nudism's to supply it

explanation.surface: Naked bathing in the sea runs riot during a late heatwave.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the fodder has only twelve letters; the setter later added 's to 'nudism' to give the thirteenth, an S.
explanation.definitionFit: These are spells of warm weather arriving late in the year, in autumn, so times of late heat.

clue.text: Underwater explorer drives madly round island

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters go around the island
madly signals the letters are thrown into wild disorder

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean island

explanation.surface: Someone driving wildly around a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' and 'round' work together: the jumbled letters are split so the island sits after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver using breathing apparatus explores beneath the sea, an underwater explorer.

clue.text: Like polo team to drink

parts.note: a crew is a team, especially of rowers
to neck is slang for drinking quickly

explanation.surface: A polo team setting out for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo neck and this round collar are both named styles of jumper neckline, so one is like the other.

clue.text: Celt to put in gun

indicators.note: put in means the second piece is placed inside the first

parts.note: the Bren is a British light machine gun

explanation.surface: A Celtic warrior is to be armed with a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Brittany belongs to one of the Celtic peoples, with a Celtic language.

clue.text: Concerned with head lice, chap scratched

indicators.note: scratched suggests things scraped and disturbed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A man with head lice is scratching himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Cephalic is the medical adjective relating to the skull or cranium.

clue.text: Plays jazz live — blow saxophone primarily

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a bop is a blow or punch

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A jazz musician performing live, blowing mainly on a saxophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Bebop is a fast, complex form of jazz, used here as a verb meaning to play that music.

clue.text: Toss butter to make stiff

parts.note: a horse that bucks tosses its rider
a ram is a butter, an animal that butts

explanation.surface: Instructions for whipping butter until it firms up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the spread but one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is coarse stiffened cloth, and figuratively means rigid or stiff in manner.

clue.text: A banker's corrupt state

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A banker's dishonest country is under attack.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the US states of the Great Plains, its capital Lincoln.

clue.text: Top record by tenor

parts.note: a single is a record with one main track

explanation.surface: A tenor's best record.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest, a garment worn on the upper body, and tops are such garments.

clue.text: Who perhaps can issue erudite wit

parts.note: Doctor Who, the TV time traveller, is one example of a doctor
john and can are both slang for a lavatory
a son is a child, one's issue

explanation.surface: A question: who might be able to produce learned humour?
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson, the eighteenth-century lexicographer, was famous for his learning and witticisms.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Johnson compiled a great dictionary and was renowned for his learned, witty remarks.

clue.text: Magician carrying off trick — one of 12

indicators.note: carrying off means the second piece is taken away from the first

parts.note: a conjuror is a stage magician
a con is a trick or swindle

explanation.surface: A magician successfully performing an illusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury in English law has twelve members, so each is one of a dozen.

clue.text: Scottish town sheltering English philosopher

indicators.note: sheltering means the first piece covers the second inside it

parts.note: Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scottish town gives refuge to an English thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A. J. Ayer was a twentieth-century British thinker, author of Language, Truth and Logic.

clue.text: Spiny anteater finally taken in by abler vet recovered

indicators.note: taken in by means the letter goes inside the jumbled letters
recovered read as re-covered, re-arranged, means the letters are reordered
finally means the last letter only is used

explanation.surface: A spiny anteater is treated by a more capable vet and gets better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recovered' turns ABLER VET into VETEBRAL; 'taken in by' places R, the last letter of anteater, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertebral means relating to the spine or backbone, hence spinal or spiny.

clue.text: Doll not PC — how surprising!

definitions.meaning: a golliwog, a black-faced rag doll now considered offensive
an old-fashioned exclamation of mild astonishment, like gosh

explanation.surface: Someone shocked to find an offensive doll on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the short form of golliwog, a now-unacceptable toy, and a mild exclamation of surprise.

clue.text: Sport with politician in historic Parliament

parts.note: RU is rugby union
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Sport and politicians mixing in an old parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rump Parliament was what remained of the Long Parliament after Pride's Purge in 1648.

clue.text: Agent for clergyman reduced men

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: reduced means the word is cut short, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a curate is an assistant clergyman
OR, other ranks, are soldiers or men

explanation.surface: A representative acting for a clergyman whose staff has been cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A procurator is a person appointed to act for another, a legal agent or proxy.
